Physical model, method, and verification

Models retained

The robot uses ṗ = v and v̇ = u + (0.1/0.680) ‖w(p) − v‖ [w(p) − v], with ±1.6 m/s² control limits. The existing whole-environment clarity dynamics and Q = 0.16 in A/B, 0.02 elsewhere are retained. The wind field is known without uncertainty.

The original relaxed RPCBF is inside proposed planning. Both methods execute the original full hard RPCBF with the same 0.06 m margin. Physics and clarity integrate every 0.01 s; execution filtering runs every 0.05 s. Infeasibility and contact remain visible.

Environment construction

Five circular column footprints follow the sketch. The uppermost column leaves a 0.30 m wall gap. The 3D D3Q19 MRT / Smagorinsky CFD calculation is rerun around these columns. Its 16–32 s vector mean defines a stationary field. Interior velocities are not painted or rescaled.

The existing finite-grid numerical wind model is provisional; full-scene convergence and experimental accuracy have not been established.

Route choice is measured

Online geometric search supplies central, lower, and upper alternatives. The original MBD optimizes every acceleration coordinate over a 15 s horizon, replanning every 5 s. No route label, named destination, method-specific penalty, or forced route selection is added to the objective.

The baseline plans in still air. The table distinguishes its predicted route from the executed route after the wind and filter act. Initial conditions vary position, velocity, clarity, and diffusion seed. All declared cases are retained.

15 s horizon · 120 free acceleration coordinates · 43 MBD search evaluations plus one retained forecast. Across completed missions, median warm planning is 311 ms (aware) / 251 ms (baseline); maximum 0.801 s. First-call compilation is separate. An earlier attempt hit 1.497 s and was stopped by the budget guard; five repetitions of that exact call took 0.187–0.198 s. The original overrun’s cause was not isolated. Timing investigation ↗
